title: Simulation & Research Platform
description: Transform the project into a serious policy experimentation platform: Monte Carlo simulation, sensitivity analysis, policy comparison, benchmarking, reproducible research exports, an authenticated API and dataset versioning.
rationale: This is the destination: rigorous, repeatable experimentation plus programmatic access, elevating the tool to something usable in research, teaching and serious analysis.
success_criteria: Monte Carlo and sensitivity analyses run over the engine and report results
Two or more saved models can be compared/benchmarked side by side
Research exports are reproducible and record engine/dataset/seed versions
A documented API exposes core capabilities under authentication
notes:
## Scope (in)
- Monte Carlo simulation
- Sensitivity analysis
- Policy comparison
- Model benchmarking
- Research exports
- API access
- Dataset versioning

## Out of scope
- New socio-economic channels (EPIC-012)
- New distributional dimensions (EPIC-013)

## Dependencies
- EPIC-012 - Monte Carlo/sensitivity need engine parameters + uncertainty
- EPIC-013 - research outputs include distributional dimensions
- EPIC-004 - comparison/benchmarking operate over saved models

## Assumptions
- The engine exposes parameters and uncertainty amenable to sampling
- Heavy computation may run asynchronously/batched
- Research exports are reproducible and cite engine/dataset versions

## Risks
- Compute cost of simulations -> async jobs, sampling budgets, caching
- Reproducibility of stochastic runs -> seeded runs; record seed + versions
- API abuse -> auth (EPIC-005), rate limits, usage tracking
- Dataset drift breaks old research -> dataset versioning; pin versions in exports

## Future extensions
- Collaborative research workspaces
- Public research dataset / model registry
- Plug-in framework for third-party analysis modules
- Reproducibility 'notebooks' bundling model + run + export
